title: A performance task needs an evidenced choice
statement: A performance task asks for a delivery choice, such as a stressed word or a pause, justified by the text's words, and accepts any choice the explanation supports.
example: One drama task scored three things, the exact word chosen, a plausible intended meaning and the link between delivery and that meaning, and accepted any word that fit.
detail: The rebuilt Grade 5 drama unit made it a release rule that a performance task must require an evidenced delivery choice, not only the selection of a fact. Its final task asks which word in a line to stress and what that emphasis helps the audience understand, and it accepts several words when the explanation fits. An audit of the independent tasks confirmed that the rubric accepts multiple defensible words rather than imitation of the model.
against: A planned delivery is not yet a performance: "It assesses performance planning; actual delivery is a separate requirement if the curriculum expects a performance." (`grade3-reading/visual-findings-2026-09-07/review-readiness/curriculum-alignment/rebuild/unit1/INDEPENDENT-TASK-AUDIT.md`, line 22).

evidence.quote: A performance task must require an evidenced delivery choice, not only selection of a fact.
Multiple keys are valid when the explanation fits. Criteria: exact chosen word, plausible intended meaning, connection between delivery and that meaning.
Rubric explicitly accepts multiple defensible words, not imitation.
